source.title: VaViM and VaVAM: Autonomous Driving through Video Generative Modeling
source.authors: Florent Bartoccioni; Elias Ramzi; Victor Besnier; S. Venkataramanan; Tuan-Hung Vu; Yi-Hong Xu; Loïck Chambon; Spyros Gidaris; Serkan Odabas; David Hurych; Renaud Marlet; Alexandre Boulch; Mickael Chen; Éloi Zablocki; Andrei Bursuc; Eduardo Valle; Matthieu Cord

record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation next-token cross-entropy scaling and extrapolation for autoregressive video models, extending scaling-law tests beyond text. It also reports how downstream driving metrics vary with model and data scale.
record.gate_note: The scaling-law fit combines checkpoints from two model widths; the text reports the fit and an error for the 1.2B model, but not the individual validation-loss values shown in Figure 5. Downstream driving results are recorded where they vary model or training-data scale. Other generation, segmentation, and safety results without a scale comparison are not included.
record.test_reason: The study fits an L0 + A·D^-α + B·N^-β law to validation next-token cross-entropy of autoregressive driving-video models and checks it against a held-out 1.2B run, a new modality for V2 and V5. It also reports downstream driving, generation and segmentation metrics across model and data scale (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that their video scaling law predicts the 1.2B model's loss within 0.06% and shows the models are under-trained, so more data should help. Larger models give better FID but worse semantic segmentation. Scaling improves open-loop minADE, but closed-loop safety does not improve consistently: collision rate tends to rise while mean deviation falls. They attribute this to imitation learning making larger models overfit to trajectory following.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a loss form with irreducible loss plus separate power-law terms for data and model size, but applies it to video clips and non-embedding parameters rather than language-model tokens and parameters. The fit uses multiple checkpoints from two widths and SciPy L-BFGS-B.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that progress varies unpredictably and collision rate tends to increase with model or data scale in closed-loop evaluation; it does not report sensitivity of the fitted loss law to alternative fitting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: From the fitted law the authors derive D = 1.384·N^0.962, close to equal scaling of data and parameters. They also state the models are under-trained relative to this frontier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Video-model compute-optimal frontier derived from a two-width fit (bears on V3 in a new modality, but untested against fixed-budget sweeps)

record.problems: The validation-loss values for individual scaling-law checkpoints and the flagship model are not stated in the text; the fit combines checkpoints from only two model widths. The extrapolation is not orders of magnitude. Closed-loop results are limited to the frontal scenario for the scale sweep, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Other outcomes not linked to the tested versions, including FID, semantic segmentation, and unscaled baseline comparisons, are not recorded.

untested.parts: Language-model loss is not studied; only video models are.
Extrapolation over orders of magnitude. The test spans about 4x in parameters (318M to 1.2B).
Compute-optimal allocation under varied fixed budgets. The D–N relation is only derived from the fitted law.
All of it; depth is fixed at 24 layers and only width varies.
Image models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. Only video pretraining loss is fitted.
Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss. Language-model tasks.
All of it; no alternative fitting choices are compared.

missing.what: Semantic segmentation mIoU vs model size for pretrained and fine-tuned VaViM S/B/L on Cityscapes, KITTI-1f and KITTI. Larger models are worse.
Generation FID@1-4 vs model size for VaViM S/B/L on KITTI and nuScenes. FID improves monotonically with size.
Per-checkpoint validation losses used for the fit, and the observed and predicted loss of the 1.2B model.

record.verdict_notes: The record omits the segmentation and FID scale comparisons, which bear on V6. The meaning of the downstream '# DATA' axis (38K-139K) is not clearly defined in the text. The parameter extrapolation is only about 4x, and the fit uses two widths, so V2 support is weak. Several rows coded partial or reversed are actually negligible changes.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses video models, not language models.
The reported extrapolation is to a 1.2B-parameter model from smaller video-model runs, not to runs orders of magnitude larger.
The study derives a data-to-parameter relationship but does not test a loss-minimising allocation under varying fixed compute budgets.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Only autoregressive video pre-training is tested; image models, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, and other modalities or regimes are not tested for this loss law.
Downstream predictability is tested for video-model driving tasks, not language-model tasks or performance as a function of pretraining loss.
The study does not compare fitting choices or setups to test whether exponents or optimal splits depend on them.

rows.operation_detail: Fit validation next-token cross-entropy against dataset size and non-embedding parameter count using checkpoints at 25%, 50%, and 75% of pre-training data.
rows.note: The fit uses checkpoints from the 185M- and 318M-parameter models; D is the number of video clips and N is non-embedding parameters.
rows.check: The fit rests on six checkpoints (25/50/75%) from only two widths, 185M and 318M. No goodness-of-fit is reported beyond the single flagship prediction.
